intro.heading: Surgical care with one dentist, start to finish
paragraphs: Oral surgery covers the procedures that go beyond a filling or a crown: removing a damaged or impacted tooth, rebuilding jawbone, clearing a stubborn infection or placing an implant. At Valencia Dentistry in Santa Clarita, these are done in the same office, by the same dentist you see for everything else. Dr. Moezzi plans each case with 3D imaging and walks you through what will happen before anything begins.

Comfort is built into the plan. Local anesthesia is standard, sedation options are offered when appropriate, and the office is quiet and unhurried. Many patients are back to their normal routine within a few days, depending on the procedure. Whether you need a single extraction or you are preparing for full-arch implants, you get a clear timeline, honest pricing and a direct line to the person who treated you.

whoItsFor.heading: Who it's for
whoItsFor.intro: Oral surgery may be the right step if any of the following sounds familiar.
items: A tooth is too damaged, decayed or infected to save
Wisdom teeth are impacted, crowding other teeth or causing pain
You have persistent tooth pain, swelling or jaw discomfort that has not resolved
You are planning dental implants and need bone rebuilt first
You have lost bone or facial support after missing teeth for some time

benefits.heading: What oral surgery can do for you
benefits.intro: Treating the problem at its source brings relief now and protects your options later.

items.title: Relief from pain and infection
items.text: Removing the cause of chronic discomfort rather than managing it indefinitely.

items.title: Better everyday function
items.text: Chew, speak and smile without working around a sore or missing tooth.

items.title: A foundation for implants
items.text: Grafting and careful extraction create the stable bone an implant needs to last.

items.title: Bone and facial structure preserved
items.text: Timely treatment limits bone loss and helps maintain the natural contours of your face.

items.title: Confidence in your smile
items.text: A healthier, more complete smile that feels like your own.

options.heading: Our oral surgery services
options.intro: Each of these is planned and performed by Dr. Moezzi in our Santa Clarita office.

items.title: Dental Implants
items.text: Permanent tooth replacements anchored in the jawbone that look and work like natural teeth.

items.title: All-on-4 Implants
items.text: A full-arch restoration supported by four strategically placed implants per jaw.

items.title: Tooth Extractions
items.text: Gentle removal of damaged, infected or crowded teeth, with socket preservation when implants are planned.

items.title: Bone Grafting
items.text: Rebuilds jawbone lost to extraction, infection or time, preparing the site for implants.

items.title: Wisdom Teeth Removal
items.text: Surgical removal of third molars that are impacted, misaligned or causing pain.

process.heading: What to expect
process.intro: A three-stage path, clearly explained, from first scan to final check.

steps.title: Consultation and digital imaging
steps.text: A comprehensive exam, a 3D CBCT scan and a careful discussion of your symptoms and goals. Dr. Moezzi reviews your options and designs a surgical plan around your anatomy and health history.

steps.title: Surgery day
steps.text: Your procedure takes place in our office under local anesthesia, with sedation if planned. Guided techniques and precise instruments keep the work efficient and the discomfort low.

steps.title: Recovery and follow-up
steps.text: You leave with written instructions and a follow-up visit on the calendar. Most patients return to normal activity within a few days, depending on the procedure, and Dr. Moezzi checks healing personally.

technology.heading: Technology in our surgical care
technology.intro: The tools on site make surgery more precise and recovery smoother.

items.title: 3D CBCT imaging
items.text: A full three-dimensional view of bone, roots, nerves and sinuses before any incision is made.

items.title: Guided surgery
items.text: Digital planning from your scan guides implant placement to the intended position and angle.

items.title: PRF therapy
items.text: Platelet-rich fibrin from your own blood is placed at the surgical site to support healing.

items.title: Laser dentistry
items.text: Used for soft-tissue work where it allows a gentler procedure with less bleeding.

aftercare.heading: Before and after surgery
before: Follow fasting instructions if sedation is planned
Pause medications only if Dr. Moezzi advises it
Arrange a ride home if you will be sedated
Avoid smoking and alcohol for at least 24 hours before your appointment
Keep up careful brushing and flossing to lower the risk of infection
after: Rest and limit physical activity for the first 24 to 48 hours
Eat soft, cool foods such as yogurt, smoothies and soup
Do not drink through a straw, smoke or spit forcefully
Use ice packs and any prescribed medication to manage swelling and discomfort
Keep the area clean with gentle brushing and saltwater rinses

cost.heading: Cost and financing
cost.text: Oral surgery costs depend on the procedure, its complexity and how your insurance plan handles surgical codes. A simple extraction and a full-arch implant case sit at very different points on that range, so we do not post single prices. After your exam and imaging, you receive a written estimate that lists each step, what your plan is expected to cover and what you would pay. We accept most major PPO plans, including Delta Dental, MetLife, Cigna, Aetna and Blue Cross Blue Shield, and we help you make the most of your benefits. Flexible financing is available for larger treatment plans.

faqs.a: Most procedures are done under local anesthesia, so you should not feel pain while the work is being done, and sedation options are available for added comfort. Afterward, some soreness and swelling is normal for a few days. Most patients tell us it was less than they had braced for, and it is managed with ice and the medication Dr. Moezzi recommends.

faqs.q: How long is recovery after oral surgery?
faqs.a: Initial recovery usually takes two to five days, depending on the procedure. That is the period for rest, soft foods and keeping the site clean. Complete healing takes longer, especially for implants and bone grafts, where the bone itself needs several weeks to a few months to mature.

faqs.q: What can I eat after oral surgery?
faqs.a: For the first few days, stay with soft foods: smoothies, yogurt, mashed potatoes, soup and scrambled eggs. Cool or lukewarm is better than hot. Avoid anything crunchy, spicy or very hot, and skip straws, until our team tells you it is fine to return to a normal diet.

faqs.q: How much does oral surgery cost?
faqs.a: It depends on the procedure and your insurance coverage. We give you a written estimate before treatment, with each step itemized and your expected insurance contribution shown. Most major PPO plans are accepted, and flexible financing is available so cost does not have to delay care you need.

faqs.q: Do you offer sedation for anxious patients?
faqs.a: Yes. Beyond local anesthesia, we offer nitrous oxide and oral sedation to help you stay relaxed during your procedure. Dr. Moezzi will discuss which option fits your health history and the length of the procedure, and explain what to arrange beforehand, such as a ride home.

faqs.q: When should wisdom teeth be removed?
faqs.a: Wisdom teeth are commonly removed between the ages of 17 and 25, when the roots are still forming and recovery tends to be easier. Removal is recommended when they are impacted, coming in at an angle, crowding other teeth or causing pain or infection. Early evaluation with a 3D scan helps avoid problems later.

faqs.q: How do I know if I need oral surgery?
faqs.a: Persistent tooth pain, swelling, jaw discomfort, a tooth that cannot be saved, or plans for dental implants are the usual reasons. The only way to know for sure is an exam and imaging. Dr. Moezzi will explain what she sees and whether surgery, a less invasive option or simply monitoring is the right call.

faqs.q: Can I get oral surgery if I have a medical condition?
faqs.a: Many patients with medical conditions can have oral surgery safely. Dr. Moezzi reviews your full health history and medication list first, and may coordinate with your physician when a condition such as diabetes or a blood thinner needs to be managed around the procedure. Precautions are built into your plan.

cta.heading: Ready to talk about oral surgery?
cta.text: A consultation includes an exam, 3D imaging and a clear plan with a written estimate. Patients come to us from across Santa Clarita, including Valencia, Stevenson Ranch, Newhall, Saugus and Canyon Country.
